title: TESS transits after January 2023 support published period changes for WASP-12 b and HAT-P-7 b and reject them for 7 of 24 tested hot-Jupiter candidates
abstract: Wang et al. (2024) reported 26 hot Jupiters with a possible constant period change (dP/dt), with data up to January 2023. We measured 13,874 transit mid-times of 364 hot Jupiters in TESS SPOC 2-min light curves from sectors 1 to 107 (2018 to October 2026). For each candidate, we fitted a constant-period model (H0) and a model with the published dP/dt (H1) to vetted pre-TESS literature epochs and TESS sectors 1 to 60. Then we compared their forecasts with the TESS transits from sector 61 onward, which the original study did not use. 166 control planets calibrated the forecast errors with a 1-min literature-time floor (robust sigma of normalised offsets 0.93). Of the 24 candidates with test data, the new transits favour the published rate for WASP-12 b (delta chi2 = -194) and HAT-P-7 b (-31). They favour a constant period for 11 candidates, and for 7 of them in all 4 analysis variants: WASP-45 b, WASP-17 b, WASP-22 b, WASP-16 b, XO-3 b, WASP-46 b and HAT-P-43 b. 15 candidates, which include WASP-4 b and WASP-19 b, stay inconclusive. For WASP-12 b, we measure dP/dt = -34.6 +/- 2.0 ms/yr (Q'* about 1.7e5). HAT-P-7 b has a stable period increase of +30.9 +/- 4.4 ms/yr, which tides cannot cause and a Romer delay of about +49 m/s/yr can. In TESS data alone, KELT-20 b shows +58 +/- 12 ms/yr. This agrees with a recent brown-dwarf companion report, but the signal depends on one 2019 sector. In 208 well-measured planets, 7 have |z| > 3 (0.6 expected). If all period changes are tidal, a stack without WASP-12 b gives Q'* > 6e6 (95%), mostly from WASP-18 b. Limitations: literature epochs come from the archive table and not from re-fitted light curves, some test sets have fewer than 10 transits, and we used no radial velocities.
